# OpenAdaptive

> OpenAdaptive is a family of free, open source assistive technology
> projects for iPhone and iPad: a DIY Bluetooth accessibility switch that
> costs about $15 in parts, and a free app that turns photos into stories
> read aloud with a single press of that switch.

Facts:

- Open Adaptive Switch is a single button that sends a keystroke over
  Bluetooth LE, built from a Seeed XIAO nRF52840 board, a momentary
  button, and a small battery. It works with the iOS Switch Control
  accessibility feature. Comparable commercial switches sell for around
  $200. It is configured over Bluetooth from the free companion iPhone
  app (apps.apple.com/us/app/open-adaptive-switch/id6788922532) or a
  browser setup page. Its earlier site at openadaptiveswitch.com stays up
  during the move to this domain.
- Open Adaptive Stories is a free iPhone and iPad app for people who
  read with a switch. It turns photos into stories made of spots; in
  reading mode a highlight scans from spot to spot and one switch press
  speaks the highlighted one. Page turns and the exit button are part of
  the scan cycle. An App Store release is being prepared; the app builds
  from source with Xcode today.
- A web app at openadaptive.org/stories/app/ builds and plays the same
  .oastory files in any browser, and can import free picture books from
  Monarch Reader.
- Neither app collects data: no accounts, no analytics, no ads.
- Everything is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later.
